plan: 2 Kings 11:1-3; 2 Chronicles 22:10-12; 2 Kings 11:4-12; 2 Chronicles 23:1-11; 2 Kings 11:13-16; 2 Chronicles 23:12-15; 2 Kings 11:17-21; 2 Chronicles 23:16-21; 2 Kings 12:1-16; 2 Chronicles 24:1-16, 17-22; 2 Kings 10:32-36

readings.title: Athalyahu's Bloody Coup
readings.subtitle: The royal seed is hidden from the adversary's wrath to preserve the legal line.
readings.text: [2 Kings 11:1] And Athalyah was the mother of Aḥazyahu. And when she saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all <dn>את</dn> the offspring of the reign of the house of Yehuḏah. [2] But Yehosheḇa, the daughter of Sovereign Yoram, sister of Aḥazyahu and wife of Yehoyaḏa the priest, took <dn>את</dn> Yo’ash son of Aḥazyah, and stole him away from among the sons of the sovereign’s sons who were put to death. So they hid him and his nurse in the bedroom, from Athalyahu, and he was not put to death. [3] And he remained with them in hiding in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for six years, while Athalyah was reigning over the land.

readings.title: The Strategic Formation
readings.subtitle: Yehoyaḏa establishes a perimeter of defense for the rightful heir.
readings.text: [2 Kings 11:4] And in the seventh year Yehoyaḏa strengthened himself, and sent and brought <dn>את</dn> the commanders of hundreds: Azaryah son of Yeroḥam, and Yishma‛ěl son of Yehoḥanan, and Azaryahu son of Oḇěḏ, and Ma‛asěyahu son of Aḏayahu, and Elishaphat son of Ziḵri, with the Karites and the runners, and brought <dn>את</dn> them into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to him. And they went about through Yehuḏah and gathered <dn>את</dn> the Lěvites from all the cities of Yehuḏah, and the chiefs of the fathers of Yisra’ěl, and they came to Yerushalayim. And he made a covenant with them and took an oath from them in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and showed <dn>את</dn> them the son of the sovereign. And all the assembly made a covenant with the sovereign in the House of <dn>Elohim</dn>. And he said to them, “See, the son of the sovereign is to reign, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has said of the sons of Daviḏ. [5] This is what you are to do: One-third of you who come in on the Sabbath, of the priests and the Lěvites, to be on guard in the sovereign’s house, gatekeepers of the thresholds; [6] and one-third at the gate of Sur, and one-third at the Gate of the Foundation, and one-third at the gate behind the runners. And you shall be on guard in the house, lest it be broken down, while all the people are in the courtyards of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [7] And let no one come into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> except the priests and those of the Lěvites who serve – they go in, for they are set-apart. But all the people are to guard the Charge of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And the two detachments of you who are going out on the Sabbath shall be on guard in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for the sovereign. [8] And you shall surround the sovereign on all sides, every man with his weapons in his hand. And whoever comes within the ranks, let him be put to death. And be with the sovereign as he goes out and as he comes in.”

readings.title: The Anointing of Yeho’ash
readings.subtitle: The priesthood officially instates the Davidic king.
readings.text: [9] So the Lěvites and all Yehuḏah did according to all that Yehoyaḏa the priest commanded. And each of them took <dn>את</dn> his men who were going in on the Sabbath, with those who were going out on the Sabbath, and came to Yehoyaḏa the priest, for Yehoyaḏa the priest did not dismiss the divisions. [10] And the priest gave the commanders of hundreds <dn>את</dn> the spears and the large and small shields which had belonged to Sovereign Daviḏ, that were in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [11] And he set all the people, every man with his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the House to the left side of the House, along by the slaughter-place and by the House, all around the sovereign. [12] And he brought out <dn>את</dn> the son of the sovereign and put on him <dn>את</dn> the diadem and <dn>את</dn> the Witness. And they set him up to reign. Then Yehoyaḏa and his sons anointed him, and they clapped their hands and said, “Let the sovereign live!”

readings.title: The Usurper's Execution
readings.subtitle: Athalyahu's illegitimate reign is brought to a definitive end.
readings.text: [2 Kings 11:13] And Athalyah heard <dn>את</dn> the noise of the people running and praising the sovereign, and she came to the people, into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [14] and looked and saw the sovereign standing by his column at the entrance, according to the ruling, and the chiefs and the trumpeters were beside the sovereign, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets, also the singers with instruments of song, and those who led in praise. And Athalyah tore her garments and cried out, “Treason! Treason!” [15] And Yehoyaḏa the priest brought out and commanded <dn>את</dn> the commanders of the hundreds, the officers of the army, and said to them, “Take <dn>את</dn> her outside the ranks, and slay with the sword <dn>את</dn> whoever follows her.” For the priest had said, “Do not let her be killed in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [16] So they laid hands on her, and she went by way of the entrance of the Horse Gate to the sovereign’s house, and was put to death there.

readings.title: Dismantling the Pagan System
readings.subtitle: The nation formally returns to YeHoVaH and eradicates the worship of Ba‛al.
readings.text: [2 Kings 11:17] And Yehoyaḏa made <dn>את</dn> a covenant between <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and the sovereign and the people, to be the people of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – also between the sovereign and the people. [18] And all the people of the land went to the house of Ba‛al, and broke <dn>את</dn> it down. They completely broke up <dn>את</dn> its slaughter-places and <dn>את</dn> images, and killed <dn>את</dn> Mattan the priest of Ba‛al before the slaughter-places. And Yehoyaḏa put the offices of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> into the hand of the priests, the Lěvites, whom Daviḏ had assigned in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to offer the ascending offerings of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, as it is written in the Torah of Mosheh, with rejoicing and with singing, by the hands of Daviḏ. And he set <dn>את</dn> the gatekeepers at the gates of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, so that no one who was in any way unclean should enter.

readings.title: The Reign Commences
readings.subtitle: Yeho’ash takes the throne, restoring structural harmony to Yerushalayim.
readings.text: [19] And he took <dn>את</dn> the commanders of hundreds, and the Karites, and the nobles, the governors of the people, and the runners, and all the people of the land. And they brought <dn>את</dn> the sovereign down from the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and went through the Upper Gate to the sovereign’s house. And they set <dn>את</dn> the sovereign on the throne of the reign. [20] And all the people of the land rejoiced. And the city had rest, for they had slain <dn>את</dn> Athalyahu with the sword in the sovereign’s house. [21] Yeho’ash was seven years old when he began to reign.

readings.title: A Reign of Incomplete Obedience
readings.subtitle: Yeho’ash follows Torah under the priest's guidance, yet the high places remain.
readings.text: [2 Kings 12:1] Yeho’ash began to reign in the seventh year of Yěhu, and he reigned forty years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Tsiḇyah of Be’ěrsheḇa. [2] And Yeho’ash did what was right in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> all the days of Yehoyaḏa the priest. [3] However, the high places were not taken away; the people still slaughtered and burned incense on the high places. And Yehoyaḏa took for him two wives, and he brought forth sons and daughters.

readings.title: Stagnation in the Ranks
readings.subtitle: The Lěvites delay the vital work of strengthening the House.
readings.text: [4] And after this it came to be that Yo’ash set his heart on restoring <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And he gathered <dn>את</dn> the priests and the Lěvites, and said to them, “Go out to the cities of Yehuḏah, and gather from all Yisra’ěl silver to repair <dn>את</dn> the House of your <dn>Elohim</dn> from year to year, and see that you hurry the matter.” But the Lěvites did not hurry it. [6] And it came to be, by the twenty-third year of Sovereign Yeho’ash, that the priests had not strengthened <dn>את</dn> the breaches of the House. [7] And Sovereign Yeho’ash called Yehoyaḏa the chief priest and the other priests, and said to them, “Why have you not strengthened <dn>את</dn> the breaches of the House? And now, do not take any more silver from your friends, but give <dn>את</dn> it for the breaches of the House.” [8] And the priests agreed that they would neither receive any more silver from the people, nor strengthen <dn>את</dn> the breaches of the House.

readings.title: Funding the Structural Integrity
readings.subtitle: A new economic protocol ensures the House of YeHoVaH is fortified.
readings.text: [9] So the sovereign commanded and they made <dn>את</dn> a chest, and set it outside at the gate of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And Yehoyaḏa the priest took a chest, and bored a hole in its lid, and set it beside the slaughter-place, on the right side as one comes into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And the priests who guarded the door put there all the silver that was brought into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [10] And it came to be, whenever they saw that there was much silver in the chest, that the sovereign’s scribe and the high priest’s officer came up and put it in bags, and counted <dn>את</dn> the silver that was found in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [11] and gave <dn>את</dn> the silver, weighed out, into the hands of those who did the work, who had the oversight of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And they paid it out to the carpenters and builders who worked on the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [12] and to stonemasons and stonecutters, and for buying timber and hewn stone to strengthen <dn>את</dn> the breach of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and for all that was paid out to strengthen the House. [13] And the workmen laboured, and the work of restoration progressed in their hands, and they established <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>Elohim</dn> to its proper form and strengthened it. And when they had finished, they brought <dn>את</dn> the rest of the silver before the sovereign and Yehoyaḏa, and they made utensils from it for the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, utensils for serving and offering, ladles and vessels of gold and silver. And they offered ascending offerings in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> continually all the days of Yehoyaḏa. [15] And they did not reckon with <dn>את</dn> the men into whose hand they gave the silver to be paid to workmen, for they acted trustworthily. [16] The silver from the trespass offerings and the silver from the sin offerings was not brought into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. It belonged to the priests.

readings.title: Returning to the Vomit
readings.subtitle: Upon Yehoyaḏa's death, the leadership rapidly corrupts the nation with idolatry.
readings.text: [15] And Yehoyaḏa was old and satisfied with days, and died, one hundred and thirty years old when he died. [16] And they buried him in the City of Daviḏ among the sovereigns, for he had done good in Yisra’ěl, both toward <dn>Elohim</dn> and <dn>His</dn> house. [17] And after the death of Yehoyaḏa the rulers of Yehuḏah came and bowed themselves to the sovereign. And the sovereign listened to them, [18] and they forsook <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of their fathers, and served the Ashěrim and the idols. And wrath came upon Yehuḏah and Yerushalayim because of their trespass. [19] And <dn>He</dn> sent prophets to them, to bring them back to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And they witnessed against them, but they did not listen.

readings.title: The Martyrdom of Zeḵaryah
readings.subtitle: The Spirit of Elohim brings a legal witness against the rebellious sovereign.
readings.text: [20] Then the Spirit of <dn>Elohim</dn> came upon Zeḵaryah son of Yehoyaḏa the priest, who stood above the people, and said to them, “Thus said <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dq>‘Why are you transgressing <dn>את</dn> the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and do not prosper? Because you have forsaken <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>He</dn> has forsaken you.’</dq> ” [21] And they conspired against him, and at the command of the sovereign they stoned him with stones in the courtyard of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [22] Thus Yo’ash the sovereign did not remember <dn>את</dn> the loving-commitment which Yehoyaḏa his father had done to him, and killed his son. And as he died, he said, “ <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does see, and repay!”

readings.title: The Diminishing Borders
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH legally withdraws protection, reducing the territory of Yisra’ěl.
readings.text: [32] In those days <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> began to cut off some in Yisra’ěl. And Ḥaza’ěl struck <dn>את</dn> them throughout all the border of Yisra’ěl, [33] from the Yarděn to the sun-rising: all <dn>את</dn> the land of Gil‛aḏ – the Gaḏites, and the Re’uḇěnites, and the Menashshehites – from Aro‛ěr, which is by the wadi Arnon, including Gil‛aḏ and Bashan. [34] And the rest of the acts of Yěhu, and all that he did, and all his might, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl? [35] So Yěhu slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Shomeron. And Yeho’aḥaz his son reigned in his place. [36] And the days that Yěhu reigned over Yisra’ěl in Shomeron were twenty-eight years.
